name: Question 18
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14040443/assets/8f023d50d11e5b6604e5fcc257e35aa4b8615e8c91f5855d10e73293720c27e4.png)

Identify the differential equation that generated the slope field above.
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14040443/assets/b6cf036f732d1cdff6f2e575b2ce082979d986416afd195282789303dcf70131.png)

Notice the following properties of the given slope field:

- First, the slopes become vertical as $y\to \pm 1.$

Of the given equations, the only equations that satisfy this condition are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{1}{(y+1)(y-1)^{2}} \\ {y}^{′} & =\frac{{y}^{2}}{{y}^{2}-1}\end{aligned}
$$

- Second, the slopes become horizontal as $y\to \pm \infty .$

Of the remaining options, the only one that gives this behavior is

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{1}{(y+1)(y-1)^{2}}.
$$

Notice that

$$
\frac{1}{(y+1)(y-1)^{2}}\to 0\,\text{as}\,y\to \pm \infty .
$$

Therefore, the slopes of the slope field for the differential equation ${y}^{′}=\frac{1}{(y+1)(y-1)^{2}}$ become horizontal as $y\to \pm \infty .$

On the other hand,

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{{y}^{2}}{{y}^{2}-1}=\frac{1}{(1-\frac{1}{{y}^{2}})}\to 1\,\text{as}\,y\to \pm \infty .
$$

Therefore, the slopes of the slope field for the differential equation ${y}^{′}=\frac{{y}^{2}}{{y}^{2}-1}$ do *not* become horizontal as $y\to \pm \infty .$

So, the correct answer is ${y}^{′}=\frac{1}{(y+1)(y-1)^{2}}.$

Question 18
?

Identify the differential equation that generated the slope field above.

a
y′=1(y−1)2
b
y′=1(y+1)(y−1)2
c
y′=yy+1
d
y′=y(y+1)2
e
y′=y2y2−1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Notice the following properties of the given slope field:

  • First, the slopes become vertical as y→±1.

    Of the given equations, the only equations that satisfy this condition are the following: y′=1(y+1)(y−1)2y′=y2y2−1

  • Second, the slopes become horizontal as y→±∞.

    Of the remaining options, the only one that gives this behavior is y′=1(y+1)(y−1)2.

    Notice that 1(y+1)(y−1)2→0asy→±∞. Therefore, the slopes of the slope field for the differential equation y′=1(y+1)(y−1)2 become horizontal as y→±∞.

    On the other hand, y′=y2y2−1=1(1−1y2)→1asy→±∞. Therefore, the slopes of the slope field for the differential equation y′=y2y2−1 do not become horizontal as y→±∞.

So, the correct answer is y′=1(y+1)(y−1)2.
